subject: Clarify uptime calculation for Aug 25 edge-routing partial degradation
messages:
From: Alex Bowman <alex@edgescale.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Partial degradation Aug 25 — latency spikes; question on SLA credits

Hi Soojin,

We observed sustained latency spikes for our API traffic routed through Redwood's us-west edge between 09:00 and 09:48 PDT on 2026-08-25. Our internal dashboards show 40-60% tail latency increases and ~7% error rate for HTTP 5xx during the window. This coincided with a third-party CDN incident (public post from CDN provider) but we also saw that a large portion of requests were routed through one single node that experienced degradation.

Before we escalate formally to procurement, can you confirm how Redwood calculates "uptime" for the purposes of the SLA in this scenario? Specifically:
- Are maintenance windows or third-party CDN outages automatically excluded?
- Is calculation per-region or global?
- If routing fallback on our side (to alternative edge nodes) did not occur, does that affect entitlement to credit?

I'm attaching a short graph and our request logs. We need to understand whether this will qualify for an SLA credit and what information you need from us to evaluate.

Thanks,
Alex Bowman
Head of Platform, EdgeScale
attachments: edge_latency_graph_20260825.png, api_logs_20260825.txt

---
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bowman <alex@edgescale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partial degradation Aug 25 — latency spikes; question on SLA credits

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and for the graphs. I can start with a quick answer and then loop in infra:

Short answer: uptime is measured per-region and per-route (see SLA section 3.1). Third-party outages are considered under our "infrastructure exclusions" unless we fail to meet our operational obligations (for example, if our routing or health-check configuration prevented a valid failover).

To evaluate eligibility for credit I need:
- The exact start/end timestamps (UTC) where you saw errors/latency
- A sample of request ids or the logs you attached (we'll map them to our access logs)
- Any timeout/health-check behavior you observed from clients that might indicate routing stuck to a degraded node

I'll route this to our routing/runtime team for a detailed post-mortem. If you'd prefer, we can set a short call this week to walk through the traces.

— Soojin
Sooj-in (Sooj) Lee
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Partial degradation Aug 25 — latency spikes; question on SLA credits

Team — we've completed the internal analysis. Summary:

- Root cause: a third-party CDN experienced a regional edge disruption; the CDN reported an incident that aligns with the window.
- Our routing behavior: per the routing logs, 78% of EdgeScale's traffic in the us-west region correctly shifted to healthy nodes, but ~22% of requests continued to target a single degraded node for the 09:00–09:48 window. That appears to have been caused by an intermittent health-check flap and a mis-evaluated health state in our load balancer (INF-4921).
- Impact: for EdgeScale's tenant traffic we saw elevated latency for ~48 minutes affecting 4.2% of their total regional requests.

Contract implications: Section 7 (Exclusions) allows third-party outage exclusion when failure is entirely outside Redwood's control, but it also states Redwood is not excluded if we fail to meet our operational responsibilities (including health-check correctness and routing). Given the evidence that our health checks failed to reassign a portion of traffic, we do not consider the entire window fully excluded.

Recommendation: offer a partial credit. Per SLA calculation rules (uptime measured per region, weighted by request volume), our preliminary calculation yields a 10% bill credit for the affected billing period. Calculation notes: 4.2% of regional request minutes impacted -> per clause 4.5 credit tiers, falls in the 5–10% bracket.

Next steps: need approval from Billing/legal to issue the credit and confirm exact credit amount on the invoice. Also propose the following remediation steps (to share with EdgeScale):
- Patch for health-check evaluation logic (INF-4921) — rolled to staging 2026-09-11, canary 2026-09-16.
- Post-deploy validation sweep and extended monitoring for two weeks.
- Offer a short technical debrief call with EdgeScale engineers.

I'll draft the customer-facing note once billing confirms the credit amount. Thoughts?

— Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
attachments: sla_policy_2024.pdf

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Bowman <alex@edgescale.com>, ops@edgescale.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Decision on Aug 25 uptime calculation and proposed credit

Alex — thanks again for the patience while we investigated. I want to be transparent about the conclusion and next steps.

Decision summary:
- We accept partial responsibility. While the originating third-party CDN had an incident, our internal routing health-checks did not fail over a subset of traffic as intended. Because our operational obligation contributed to the impact, we will not treat the full event as an exclusion.

Credit offered:
- A one-time credit equal to 10% of the billed usage for the affected billing period for EdgeScale's us-west regional traffic. This matches our internal calculation and Marissa's recommendation.
- If you prefer a fixed invoice credit instead of percent, we can convert to the dollar amount on the upcoming invoice (we estimate ~$4,200 for the period; final number to be confirmed by billing).

Remediation and safeguards:
- Health-check fix (INF-4921) scheduled to complete canary 2026-09-16; full rollout to follow.
- We will run an extended validation sweep and provide a short technical debrief with your platform engineers (propose Thu 2026-09-17 10:00 PDT).
- We'll add an additional alerting rule that tracks per-tenant request skew to individual edge nodes to detect this pattern earlier.

Attachments: remediation_plan_20260914.pdf (contains timelines), our internal incident summary, and copies of the logs we used for evaluation.

If this resolution is acceptable we'll route the credit through Billing and confirm the final invoice adjustment within 5 business days. Please reply to confirm acceptance or to request a short call.

Apologies for the disruption and thanks for working with us on the analysis.

Best,
Sooj
